statements.subject: mqtt
statements.description: However, MQTT v5.0 is the RECOMMENDED version, as it works more naturally with ACE-style authentication and authorization.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: To provide communication confidentiality and Broker authentication to the MQTT Clients, TLS is used, and TLS 1.3 [RFC8446] is RECOMMENDED.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The token MAY be an opaque reference to authorization information or a JSON Web Token (JWT) [RFC7519].

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: The Client-AS and RS-AS exchanges MAY also use protocols other than HTTP, e.g., Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP) [RFC7252] or MQTT.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: It is recommended that TLS is used to secure these communication channels between Client-AS and RS-AS.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: To reduce the protocol memory and bandwidth requirements, implementations MAY also use the "application/ace+cbor" content type, Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) encoding [RFC8949], CBOR Web Tokens (CWTs) [RFC8392], and associated PoP semantics.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Topic Filters may include wildcards.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The C-AS and Broker-AS communications MAY be implemented using protocols other than HTTPS, e.g., CoAP or MQTT.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Whatever protocol is used for the C-AS and Broker-AS communications MUST provide mutual authentication, confidentiality protection, and integrity protection.
statements.post_cond: channel.mutual_authentication = true & channel.confidentiality_protection = true & channel.integrity_protection = true
actions: enforce_mutual_authentication_on_channel
enforce_confidentiality_protection_on_channel
enforce_integrity_protection_on_channel

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Client and the AS MUST perform mutual authentication.
actions: Client authenticates AS
AS authenticates Client

statements.subject: mqtt
statements.description: As explained earlier, implementations MAY also use the "application/ace+cbor" content type.

statements.subject: mqtt
statements.description: This document follows [RFC7800] for PoP semantics for JWTs (CWTs MAY also be used).

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The JWT is created as explained in Section 7 of [RFC7519], and the JWT MUST include a JSON Web Encryption (JWE) [RFC7516].

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If a CWT/COSE is used, this information MUST be inside the "COSE_Key" object and MUST be encrypted using a "COSE_Encrypt0" structure.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When CBOR is used, the interactions MUST implement the procedure described in Section 5.8.3 of the ACE framework [RFC9200].
actions: implement error response procedure per ACE framework Section 5.8.3

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: Unless the Client publishes and subscribes to only public topics, the Client and the Broker MUST perform mutual authentication.
actions: perform mutual authentication between Client and Broker

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST authenticate to the Broker either over MQTT or TLS before performing any other action.
actions: authenticate to Broker via MQTT or TLS
defer all other actions until authentication is complete

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The token is transported inside the CONNECT packet and MUST be validated using one of the methods described in Section 2.2.2.
actions: validate token contained in CONNECT packet using a defined validation method

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For the RPK, the Client MUST have published the token to the "authz-info" topic.
actions: publish token to authz-info topic before initiating RPK-based TLS authentication

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For the PSK, the token MAY be published to the "authz-info" topic or MAY be, alternatively, provided as a "PSK identity" (e.g., an "identity" in the "identities" field in the Client's "pre_shared_key" extension in TLS 1.3).
actions: optionally publish token to authz-info topic
or optionally provide token as PSK identity in TLS pre_shared_key extension

statements.subject: client
statements.description: This option SHOULD NOT be chosen as the token transported in the CONNECT packet and overwrites any permissions passed during the TLS authentication.
actions: avoid selecting TLS:Known(RPK/PSK),MQTT:ace authentication combination

statements.subject: client
statements.description: It is RECOMMENDED that the Client implements TLS:Anon,MQTT:ace as the first choice when working with protected topics.
actions: prefer TLS:Anon,MQTT:ace as primary authentication method for protected topics

statements.subject: client
statements.description: However, MQTT v3.1.1 Clients that do not prefer to overload the User Name and Password fields for ACE (as described in Section 6) MAY implement TLS:Known(RPK/PSK),MQTT:none and, consequently, TLS:Anon,MQTT:None to submit their token to "authz-info".
actions: optionally implement TLS:Known(RPK/PSK),MQTT:none
optionally implement TLS:Anon,MQTT:None for authz-info token submission

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST support TLS:Anon,MQTT:ace.
actions: support TLS:Anon,MQTT:ace as a client authentication method

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To support Clients with different capabilities, the Broker MAY provide multiple client authentication options, e.g., support TLS:Known(RPK),MQTT:none and TLS:Anon,MQTT:None, to enable RPK-based client authentication.
actions: optionally provide multiple client authentication options beyond TLS:Anon,MQTT:ace

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST authenticate the Broker during the TLS handshake.
actions: authenticate Broker during TLS handshake

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Otherwise, to authenticate the Broker, the Client MUST validate a public key from an X.509 certificate or an RPK from the Broker against the "rs_cnf" parameter in the token response, which contains information about the public key used by the RS to authenticate if the token type is "pop" and asymmetric keys are used as defined in [RFC9201].
statements.pre_cond: auth.tls_method != TLS:Known(RPK/PSK) & token.type = pop & token.key_type = asymmetric
actions: validate broker X.509 public key or RPK against rs_cnf parameter in token response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The AS MAY include the thumbprint of the RS's X.509 certificate in the "rs_cnf" (thumbprint, as defined in [RFC9360]).
actions: optionally include RS X.509 certificate thumbprint in rs_cnf of token response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In this case, the Client MUST validate the RS certificate against this thumbprint.
actions: validate RS X.509 certificate against thumbprint present in rs_cnf

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The "authz-info" topic MUST only be published (i.e., the Clients are not allowed to subscribe to it).
actions: reject SUBSCRIBE requests targeting authz-info topic

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST verify the validity of the token (i.e., through local validation or introspection if the token is a reference), as described in Section 2.2.5.
actions: validate token via local validation or introspection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the token is not valid, the Broker MUST discard the token.
actions: discard token

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the QoS level is equal to 0, and the token is not valid, or if the claims cannot be obtained in the case of an introspected token, the Broker MUST send a DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x87 (Not authorized).
statements.trigger: PUBLISH received on authz-info & QoS=0 & (token.valid=false | token.claims_obtainable=false)
actions: send DISCONNECT with reason code 0x87

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the PUBLISH Payload does not parse to a token, the Broker MUST send a DISCONNECT with reason code 0x99 (Payload format invalid).
statements.trigger: PUBLISH received on authz-info & payload.parse_error=true & QoS=0
actions: send DISCONNECT with reason code 0x99

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the QoS level of the PUBLISH packet is greater than or equal to 1, and the token is not valid, or the claims cannot be obtained in the case of an introspected token, the Broker MUST send reason code 0x87 (Not authorized) in the PUBACK or PUBREC.
statements.trigger: PUBLISH received on authz-info & QoS>=1 & (token.valid=false | token.claims_obtainable=false)
actions: send PUBACK or PUBREC with reason code 0x87

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TLS 1.2 implementations MUST use the "Extended Main Secret" extension (terminology adopted from [TLS-bis]) to incorporate the handshake transcript into the main secret [RFC7627].
actions: Use Extended Main Secret extension to incorporate handshake transcript into main secret per RFC7627

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TLS implementations SHOULD use the Server Name Indication (SNI) [RFC6066] and Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) [RFC7301] extensions so the TLS handshake authenticates as much of the protocol context as possible.
actions: Use SNI extension per RFC6066
Use ALPN extension per RFC7301

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST upload the access token to the Broker using the method specified in Section 2.2.2 before initiating the handshake.
actions: upload_access_token_to_broker_via_section_2.2.2_method

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When using a previously uploaded token, the Client MUST indicate during the handshake which previously uploaded access token it intends to use.
actions: indicate previously uploaded access token identity during TLS handshake

statements.subject: client
statements.description: To do so, it MUST create a "COSE_Key" or "JWK" structure with the "kid" that was conveyed in the "rs_cnf" claim in the token response from the AS and the key type "symmetric".

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In contrast to the DTLS profile for ACE [RFC9202], a Client MAY omit support for the cipher suites TLS_PSK_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8 and TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CCM_8.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For TLS 1.2, however, a client MUST support TLS_ECDHE_PSK_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 for PSKs [RFC8442] and TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 for RPKs [RFC8422], as recommended in [RFC9325] (and adjusted to be a PSK cipher suite as appropriate).

statements.subject: client
statements.description: After sending the CONNECT packet, the Client MUST wait to receive the CONNACK packet from the Broker.
actions: await_CONNACK_from_broker

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Similarly, except for a DISCONNECT and AUTH response from the Client, the Broker MUST NOT process any packets before sending a CONNACK packet.
statements.pre_cond: server.CONNACK_sent = false & received_packet.type != DISCONNECT & received_packet.type != AUTH

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Table 1 shows how the flags MUST be set to use AUTH packets for authentication and authorization, i.e., the User Name Flag and Password Flag MUST be set to 0.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An MQTT v5.0 Broker MAY also support token transport using the User Name and Password to provide a security option for MQTT v3.1.1 Clients, as described in Section 6.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MAY set the Will Flag as desired (marked as "X" in Table 1).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Will Flag is set to 1, the Broker MUST check that the token allows the publication of the Will Message (i.e., the Will Topic Filter is in the scope array).
actions: verify_token_scope_covers_will_topic_filter

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In this profile, the Client SHOULD always start with a new Session.
actions: set_Clean_Start_flag_to_1_in_CONNECT

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MAY also signal that it does not support the continuation of an existing Session by setting the Session Expiry Interval to 0 in the CONNACK.
actions: set_Session_Expiry_Interval_to_0_in_CONNACK

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Broker starts a new Session, the Broker MUST set the Session Present flag to 0 in the CONNACK packet to signal this to the Client.
actions: set_Session_Present_flag_to_0_in_CONNACK

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MAY support continuing an existing Session, e.g., if the Broker requires it for QoS reasons.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In this case, if a CONNECT packet is received with Clean Start set to 0, and there is a Session associated with the Client Identifier, the Broker MUST resume communications with the Client based on the state from the existing Session.
actions: resume_communications_from_existing_session_state

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In its response, the Broker MUST set the Session Present flag to 1 in the CONNACK packet to signal the continuation of an existing Session to the Client.
actions: set_Session_Present_flag_to_1_in_CONNACK

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When reconnecting to a Broker that supports continuing existing Sessions, the Client MUST still provide a token in addition to using the same Client Identifier and setting the Clean Start to 0.
actions: include_token_in_CONNECT
set_same_Client_Identifier_in_CONNECT
set_Clean_Start_to_0_in_CONNECT

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST still perform PoP validation on the provided token.
actions: perform_PoP_validation_on_provided_token

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the token matches the stored state, the Broker MAY skip introspecting a token-by-reference and use the stored introspection result.
actions: use_stored_introspection_result

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST also verify the Client is authorized to receive or send MQTT packets that are pending transmission.
actions: verify_client_authorization_for_pending_mqtt_packets

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Brokers SHOULD implement administrative policies to limit misuse.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Given that the Broker MUST associate the Client with a valid token, a Client will only send or receive messages to its authorized topics.
actions: associate_client_with_valid_token

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST set the Authentication Method as a property of a CONNECT packet by using the property identifier 21 (0x15).
statements.trigger: Client initiates connection with AUTH property
actions: Include Authentication Method property (identifier 0x15) in CONNECT packet

statements.subject: message
statements.description: This is followed by a UTF-8-encoded string containing the name of the Authentication Method, which MUST be set to "ace".
actions: Set Authentication Method string value to 'ace' in CONNECT packet

statements.subject: server
statements.description:
Based on the Authentication Data, the Broker MUST support both options below:
   *  proof of possession using a challenge from the TLS session
   *  proof of possession via a Broker-generated challenge/response
actions: Accept proof-of-possession via TLS session challenge
Accept proof-of-possession via Broker-generated challenge/response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: For this option, the Authentication Data inside the Client's CONNECT packet MUST contain the two-byte integer token length, the token, and the keyed message digest (MAC) or the Client signature (as shown in Figure 3).
statements.trigger: Client sends CONNECT with PoP TLS-exporter option
actions: Include two-byte integer token length in Authentication Data field of CONNECT
Include token in Authentication Data field of CONNECT
Include keyed message digest (MAC) or Client signature over TLS exporter content in Authentication Data field of CONNECT

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Authentication Data inside the Client's CONNECT contains only the two-byte integer token length and the token (as shown in Figure 4), the Broker MUST respond with an AUTH packet with the authenticated reason code set to 0x18 (Continue Authentication).
actions: send AUTH packet with reason code 0x18 (Continue Authentication)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Authentication Method MUST be set to "ace", and the Authentication Data MUST NOT be empty and MUST contain an 8-byte RS nonce as a challenge for the Client (Figure 5).
actions: set Authentication Method field to "ace" in Broker AUTH packet

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MAY also reauthenticate using this challenge-response flow, as described in Section 4.
actions: initiate challenge-response reauthentication flow as described in Section 4

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST verify the validity of the token either locally (e.g., in the case of a self-contained token) or MAY send a request to the introspection endpoint of the AS (as described for HTTP-based interactions in Section 5.9 of the ACE framework [RFC9200]).
actions: verify_token_validity

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST verify the claims in the access token according to the rules set in Section 5.10.1.1 of the ACE framework [RFC9200].
actions: verify_token_claims

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For self-contained tokens, the Broker MUST process the security protection of the token first, as specified by the respective token format, i.e., a CWT uses COSE, while a JWT uses JOSE.
actions: process_token_security_protection_first

statements.subject: server
statements.description: HMAC-SHA-256 (HS256) [RFC6234] and Ed25519 [RFC8032] are mandatory to implement for the Broker.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST implement at least one of them depending on the choice of symmetric or asymmetric validation.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Validation of the signature or MAC MUST fail if the signature algorithm is set to "none" when the key used for the signature algorithm cannot be determined or the computed and received signature/MAC do not match.
statements.pre_cond: signature.algorithm = none | token.signing_key.undetermined = true | signature.computed != signature.received
actions: fail_signature_or_mac_validation

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST check if the access token is still valid, if it is the intended destination (i.e., the audience) of the token, and if the token was issued by an authorized Authorization Server.
statements.post_cond: token.not_expired = true & token.audience_valid = true & token.issuer_authorized = true
actions: check_token_expiry
check_token_audience
check_token_issuer_authorization

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The "cnf" claim MUST contain either the Client's RPK or, if the key is already known by the Broker (e.g., from previous communication), a reference to it.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Therefore, the token or its introspection result MUST be cached to allow a Client's future PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE messages.
actions: cache_token_or_introspection_result

statements.subject: server
statements.description: During the CONNECT, if the Will Flag is set to 1, the Broker MUST also authorize the publication of the Will Topic and Will Message using the token's scope field.
actions: authorize_Will_Topic_publication_using_token_scope
authorize_Will_Message_publication_using_token_scope

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MAY signal in the CONNACK explicitly whether Wildcard Subscriptions are supported by returning a CONNACK property "Wildcard Subscription Available".
actions: set_CONNACK.Wildcard_Subscription_Available_property

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For the authorization to succeed, the Broker MUST verify that the Topic Name or Topic Filter in question is either an exact match to or a subset of at least one "topic_filter" in the scope.
actions: verify_topic_name_or_filter_is_exact_match_or_subset_of_scope_topic_filter

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Based on the validation result (obtained either via local inspection or using the introspection interface of the AS), the Broker MUST send a CONNACK packet to the Client.
actions: send CONNACK packet to Client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MAY also trigger AS discovery and include a User Property (identified as property type 38 (0x26)) in the CONNACK for the AS Request Creation Hints.
actions: trigger_AS_discovery
include_User_Property_type_0x26_in_CONNACK_with_AS_Request_Creation_Hints

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The name of the User Property MUST be set to "ace_as_hint".

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Broker starts a new Session, it MUST also set Session Present to 0 in the CONNACK packet to signal a new Session to the Client.
actions: Set CONNACK reason code to 0x00 (Success)
Set Session Present flag to 0 in CONNACK packet
Send CONNACK to Client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Otherwise, it MUST set Session Present to 1.
actions: Set Session Present flag to 1 in CONNACK packet
Send CONNACK to Client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Having accepted the connection, the Broker MUST be prepared to store the token during the connection and after disconnection for future use.
actions: Store access token for the lifetime of the connection
Retain stored token after disconnection for future use

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the token is not self-contained and the Broker uses token introspection, it MAY cache the validation result to authorize the subsequent PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE packets.
actions: Cache token introspection validation result for subsequent PUBLISH and SUBSCRIBE authorization

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The Broker SHOULD also use a cache timeout to introspect tokens regularly.
actions: Start cache timeout timer for introspection result
Re-introspect token when cache timeout expires

statements.subject: server
statements.description: On receiving the PUBLISH packet, the Broker MUST use the type of packet (i.e., PUBLISH) and the Topic Name in the packet header to match against the scope array items in the cached token or its introspection result.
actions: match PUBLISH packet type and Topic Name against scope array items in cached token or introspection result

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the case of an authorization failure, the Broker MUST return an error if the Client has set the QoS level of the PUBLISH packet to greater than or equal to 1.
actions: send PUBACK or PUBREC with reason code 0x87 (Not authorized)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: On receiving an acknowledgment with 0x87 (Not authorized), the Client MAY reauthenticate by providing a new token, as described in Section 4.
actions: reauthenticate by providing a new token

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For all QoS levels, the Broker MAY return 0x80 (Unspecified error) if they do not want to leak the Topic Names to unauthorized clients.
actions: return reason code 0x80 (Unspecified error) instead of 0x87

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST NOT forward messages to unauthorized subscribers.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: To avoid silently dropping messages, the Broker MUST close the Network Connection and SHOULD inform the affected subscribers.
actions: close Network Connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Therefore, the Broker SHOULD send a DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x87 (Not authorized) before closing the Network Connection to these clients.
actions: send DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x87 (Not authorized)
close Network Connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: On receiving the SUBSCRIBE packet, the Broker MUST use the type of packet (i.e., SUBSCRIBE) and the Topic Filter in the packet header to match against the scope field of the stored token or introspection result.
actions: extract packet type (SUBSCRIBE) and Topic Filter from received packet header
match packet type and Topic Filter against scope field of stored token or introspection result

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Topic Filters MUST be an exact match to or be a subset of at least one of the "topic_filter" fields in the scope array found in the Client's token.
actions: authorize Topic Filter only if it exactly matches or is a subset of at least one topic_filter field in the Client token scope array

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MAY return 0x80 (Unspecified error) if they do not want to leak the Topic Names to unauthorized clients.
actions: return 0x80 (Unspecified error) in SUBACK instead of 0x87 to avoid leaking Topic Names to unauthorized clients

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST check for token expiration whenever a CONNECT, PUBLISH, or SUBSCRIBE packet is received or sent.
statements.trigger: CONNECT_received | PUBLISH_received | SUBSCRIBE_received | CONNECT_sent | PUBLISH_sent | SUBSCRIBE_sent
actions: check_token_expiration

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker SHOULD check for token expiration on receiving a PINGREQ packet.
actions: check_token_expiration

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MAY also check for token expiration periodically, e.g., every hour.
actions: check_token_expiration

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MAY reauthenticate a response to PUBACK and SUBACK, which signal loss of authorization.
actions: initiate_reauthentication

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Clients MAY also proactively update their tokens, i.e., before they receive a packet with a "Not authorized" return code.
actions: update_token_proactively

statements.subject: client
statements.description: To start reauthentication, the Client MUST send an AUTH packet with reason code 0x19 (Reauthentication).
actions: send AUTH packet with reason code 0x19 (Reauthentication)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST set the Authentication Method as "ace" and transport the new token in the Authentication Data.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If reauthenticating during the current TLS session, the Client MUST NOT use the method described in Section 2.2.4.2.1, i.e., proof of possession using a challenge from the TLS session, to avoid reusing the same challenge value from the TLS-Exporter.
actions: do not use TLS-Exporter PoP method (Section 2.2.4.2.1)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For reauthentications in the same TLS-session, the Client MUST use the challenge-response PoP, as defined in Section 2.2.4.2.2.
actions: use challenge-response PoP as defined in Section 2.2.4.2.2

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Otherwise, the Broker MUST deny the request.
actions: deny reauthentication request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the reauthentication fails, the Broker MUST send a DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x87 (Not Authorized).
actions: send DISCONNECT packet with reason code 0x87 (Not Authorized)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the case of a Client DISCONNECT, if the Session Expiry Interval is set to 0, the Broker doesn't store the Session State but MUST keep the retained messages.
actions: discard Session State
keep retained messages

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the Broker stores the Session State, the state MAY include the token and its introspection result (for reference tokens) in addition to the MQTT Session State.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The token/introspection state is not part of the MQTT Session State, and PoP validation is required for each new connection, regardless of whether existing MQTT Sessions are continued.
actions: perform PoP validation before completing connection establishment

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST continue publishing the retained messages as long as the associated tokens are valid.
actions: continue publishing retained messages while token is valid

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Therefore, the Broker MUST use the minimum of the token expiry and message expiry interval to discard a retained message.
actions: set discard timer to min(token_expiry_interval, message_expiry_interval)
discard retained message on timer expiry

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client's token scope array MUST include the Will Topic.
actions: validate that token scope includes Will Topic

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Will Message MUST be published to the Will Topic, regardless of whether the corresponding token has expired (as it has been validated and accepted during CONNECT).
actions: publish Will Message to Will Topic irrespective of token expiry state

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An MQTT v5.0 Broker MAY implement these interactions for the MQTT v3.1.1 Clients; the flows described in this section are NOT RECOMMENDED for use by MQTT v5.0 Clients.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: As in MQTT v5.0, the token MAY either be transported before, by publishing to the "authz-info" topic, or inside the CONNECT packet.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the Client provided the token via the "authz-info" topic and will not update the token in the CONNECT packet, it MUST authenticate over TLS.
actions: authenticate over TLS

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker SHOULD still be prepared to store the Client access token for future use (regardless of the method of transport).
actions: store client access token for future use

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Table 2 shows how the MQTT connect flags MUST be set to initiate a connection with the Broker.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client SHOULD set the Clean flag to 1 to always start a new Session.
actions: set Clean flag = 1 in CONNECT packet

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Clean flag is set to 0, the Broker MUST resume communications with the Client based on the state from the current Session (as identified by the Client Identifier).
actions: resume communications based on current Session state identified by Client Identifier

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If there is no Session associated with the Client Identifier, the Broker MUST create a new Session.
actions: create new Session

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST set the Session Present flag in the CONNACK packet accordingly, i.e., 0 to indicate a new Session to the Client and 1 to indicate that the existing Session is continued.
actions: set Session Present = 0 in CONNACK if new Session
set Session Present = 1 in CONNACK if existing Session is continued

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker MUST still perform PoP validation on the provided Client token.
actions: perform PoP validation on provided client token

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MAY set the Will Flag as desired (marked as "X" in Table 2).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: User Name and Password flags MUST be set to 1 to ensure that the Payload of the CONNECT packet includes both the User Name and Password fields.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: To signal that the User Name field contains an ACE token, this field MUST be prefixed with the keyword "ace", i.e., the User Name field is a concatenation of 'a', 'c', 'e', and the access token represented as:

statements.subject: message
statements.description: To this end, the access token MUST be encoded with base64url, omitting the "=" padding characters [RFC4648].

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Password field MUST be set to the keyed message digest (MAC) or signature associated with the access token for PoP.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The Client MUST apply the PoP key on the challenge derived from the TLS session, as described in Section 2.2.4.2.1.
actions: apply PoP key on challenge derived from TLS session

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The tokenless CONNECT attempt MUST fail.
actions: reject CONNECT attempt

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the case of an authorization error, the Broker MUST ignore the PUBLISH packet and disconnect the Client.
actions: ignore PUBLISH packet
disconnect Client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: These token expirations MUST lead to disconnecting the Client rather than silently dropping messages.
actions: disconnect Client

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the Broker caches the token introspection responses, then the Broker SHOULD use a reasonable cache timeout to introspect tokens regularly.
actions: set cache timeout to a reasonable value
re-introspect tokens at regular intervals defined by cache timeout

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Broker SHOULD implement administrative policies to limit misuse by the Client resulting from continuing existing Sessions.
actions: enforce administrative policies to detect and limit Client misuse within continuing Sessions

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In MQTT, the Broker is a central trusted party and may forward potentially sensitive information between Clients.

statements.subject: mqtt
statements.description: This functionality may be implemented using the proposal outlined in the ACE Pub-Sub Profile [ACE-PUBSUB-PROFILE].

statements.subject: server
statements.description: authz-info endpoint: It MAY be supported using the method described in Section 2.2.2 but is not protected other than by the TLS channel between the Client and RS.
